title: OM Quiz — Block 4: Supply Chain Management

examInfo.format: 12 Single Choice + 4 Multiple Choice (Prüfungsstil, mit Rechenfragen)
examInfo.grading: Übungsset ohne Note — Ziel: ≥ 60 % der Punkte

questions.text: The bullwhip effect describes the amplification of demand variability…

choices.text: from the manufacturer downstream towards the end customer
only within the retail store
only in supply chains with a single stage
from the end customer upstream towards the manufacturer and suppliers

questions.explanation: Bullwhip = Verstärkung der Schwankungen entgegen dem Warenfluss (upstream): kleine Schwankungen beim Endkunden führen zu grossen Bestellschwankungen beim Hersteller und Zulieferer.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the main drivers of the bullwhip effect?

choices.text: Unused production capacity
Order batching
Price fluctuations and promotions
Rationing and shortage gaming

questions.explanation: Haupttreiber: Demand Signal Processing/Forecast Updating, Order Batching, Price Fluctuations, Rationing & Gaming. Leerkapazität gehört nicht dazu.

questions.text:
The variance of the customer demand is 25 and the variance of the orders placed at the manufacturer is 150.

How large is the bullwhip effect?

An order-up-to policy sets the target inventory T. In week 1 the target is 120 units, in week 2 it is 150 units. The actual demand in week 2 is 100 units.

How many units are ordered in week 2 (order = demand + change of the target)?

choices.text: 100 units
130 units
150 units
250 units

questions.explanation: Bestellung = D + (T2 − T1) = 100 + (150 − 120) = 130. Die Änderung des Zielbestands (Prognose-Update) verstärkt die Bestellvarianz gegenüber der Nachfragevarianz.

questions.text:
Two independent markets have a demand standard deviation of 60 and 80 units per week.

How large is the standard deviation of the pooled demand (postponement)?
questions.explanation: σ_pool = √(60² + 80²) = √10'000 = 100. Varianzen addieren sich, nicht die Standardabweichungen (140 wäre die Summe).

questions.text:
Same data (σ = 60 and 80, pooled σ = 100). The safety stock is proportional to σ (same service level z).

By how much does the total safety stock fall with postponement?

choices.text: about 10 %
about 28.6 %
about 50 %
about 14.3 %

questions.explanation: Einsparung = 1 − 100/(60 + 80) = 1 − 0.714 = 28.6 %. Bei vier gleichen unabhängigen Märkten wären es 50 % (1 − 1/√4).

questions.text:
Postponement newsvendor: holding cost h = CHF 20 and penalty cost p = CHF 60 per unit and week.

What is the critical ratio CR = p/(p + h) used for z*?
questions.explanation: CR = 60/(60 + 20) = 0.75 ⇒ z* = NORM.S.INV(0.75) = 0.674. Die Rollen von h und p nicht vertauschen (0.25).

questions.text: Which Excel function returns the density φ(z) of the standard normal distribution, as needed for f01(z*) in the postponement cost formula?

choices.text: NORM.S.DIST(z; FALSE)
NORM.S.INV(z)
NORM.S.DIST(z; TRUE)
NORM.DIST(z; 0; 1; TRUE)

questions.explanation: FALSE = Dichte (Höhe der Kurve), TRUE = Verteilungsfunktion (Fläche). NORM.S.INV ist die Umkehrfunktion (Quantil).

questions.text:
Inventory simulation: Day 1: begin inventory 20, receipt 0, demand 15. Day 2: demand 10, receipt 0. Day 3: receipt 30, demand 12. Demand filled = MIN(available, demand).

How many units of demand are lost (stockout) over the three days?

choices.text: 0 units
5 units
10 units
15 units

questions.explanation: Tag 1: Ende 5. Tag 2: verfügbar 5, Nachfrage 10 ⇒ gefüllt 5, Stockout 5, Ende 0. Tag 3: verfügbar 30, Nachfrage 12 ⇒ Ende 18, kein Stockout. Total 5.

questions.text:
A bootstrap analysis gives an 80 % confidence interval of [−0.4, 2.6] for the difference Δ = (new machine − old machine) of parts per cycle.

What is the sensible decision?

choices.text: No decision is possible, because bootstrap results are random
Switch to the new machine, because the interval is wider than 2
Switch to the new machine, because the upper limit is above 0
Keep the old machine, because the lower limit is below 0

questions.explanation: Wechsel nur, wenn die untere KI-Grenze > 0 ist. Hier −0.4 < 0 ⇒ nicht eindeutig besser ⇒ alte Maschine behalten. Wegen der Zufälligkeit mehrfach rechnen.

questions.text: Which product and demand situation fits an agile (responsive) supply chain best?

choices.text: Commodity products with stable, predictable demand
Products with a single customer and fixed annual volumes
Innovative products with short life cycle and volatile demand
Standardised bulk goods with minimal stock goals

questions.explanation: Agile: volatile Nachfrage, innovative Produkte, Reaktionsfähigkeit, Pull/Kundenauftrag. Lean passt zu stabiler Nachfrage und Commodities (Effizienz).

questions.text: In a dependent-sample bootstrap (same machines before and after an upgrade), what is resampled?

choices.text: The mean of the sample, without replacement
Only the before-values
The per-machine differences (after − before), drawn with replacement
The two groups separately and independently

questions.explanation: Bei abhängigen Stichproben (gepaart) werden die Differenzen pro Einheit gebildet und resampled. Bei unabhängigen Gruppen werden beide Gruppen getrennt resampled.

sections.title: Part B – Multiple Choice (4 Points)
sections.description: At least two answers are correct. Only the complete correct combination scores (no partial points).

questions.text: Which statements about the bullwhip effect are correct?

choices.text: Price promotions can trigger forward buying and thus amplify it.
It can be measured as Var(orders) / Var(demand).
It is mainly caused by unused production capacity.
It moves downstream from the manufacturer to the consumer.
Sharing point-of-sale data along the chain reduces it.

questions.explanation: Kennzahl Var(Orders)/Var(Demand) > 1; POS-Datenaustausch reduziert Demand Signal Processing; Promotionen verursachen Vorratskäufe. Leerkapazität ist kein Treiber; der Effekt läuft upstream.

questions.text: Which measures help to reduce the bullwhip effect?

choices.text: Shorter lead times
Larger and rarer batch orders to the supplier
Coordinating the demand forecasts of the companies in the chain
Stable prices instead of frequent promotions (every-day-low-price)
Reducing the order lot sizes

questions.explanation: Koordinierte Prognosen (CPFR), kleinere Bestelllose, stabile Preise, kürzere Lieferzeiten dämpfen den Effekt. Grosse, seltene Batch-Bestellungen verstärken ihn.

questions.text: Which statements about postponement are correct?

choices.text: The pooled standard deviation of independent markets is √(σ1² + σ2² + … + σn²).
It increases the required safety stock because uncertainties of the markets simply add up.
It allows flexible reaction to demand fluctuations in different sub-markets.
It shifts the product configuration point towards the customer.
It reduces the total safety stock needed.

questions.explanation: Postponement: späte Differenzierung ⇒ Risk Pooling: σ_pool = √Σσ² < Σσ ⇒ weniger Sicherheitsbestand. Die Aussage «Unsicherheiten addieren sich» ist falsch (HS23 Q21).

questions.text: Which statements about supply chain simulation and bootstrap are correct?

choices.text: Supply chains cannot always be optimised analytically; simulation is often necessary.
Bootstrap resamples the observed data with replacement.
Demand filled in a daily simulation equals MIN(available inventory, demand).
The stockout in a daily simulation equals MIN(available inventory, demand).
A single simulation run is a random result; several runs should be evaluated.

questions.explanation: Simulation (Monte Carlo) bei nicht analytisch lösbaren Ketten; mehrfach laufen lassen; Bootstrap = Ziehen mit Zurücklegen; Demand Filled = MIN(Verfügbar, Nachfrage), Stockout = MAX(0, Nachfrage − Verfügbar).
